taxonomy.note: Canonical genus corrected from source-pool Panicum obtusum to current Hopia obtusa. Panicum obtusum remains an important field-guide synonym.

evidence: Kew/POWO accepts Hopia obtusa and lists Texas in its native range; Panicum obtusum is a homotypic synonym.
The project Hays County native source pool records the taxon under Panicum obtusum.
The Balcones Canyonlands Preserve plant list explicitly records vine mesquite (Panicum obtusum) in Travis County.
The Texas Hill Country grass treatment documents Hopia obtusa as a widespread Hill Country species; Blanco County is retained from the project's reviewed Hill Country source set.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Occurrence is not treated as nativity; introduced records do not count toward the three-county native threshold.

morphology.look_here_first: Ignore the old Panicum label and look at the runners: long wiry stolons with swollen woolly nodes root to make new plants, while narrow upright seedheads rise from the sod.
diagnostic_traits: stolon nodes swollen, villous/woolly and rooting
culms 20–60 cm from a hard knotty base
inflorescence with 1–4 short appressed raceme-like branches

confusers.separator: Switchgrass forms tall rhizomatous clumps and lacks the long rooting stolons with woolly nodes.
Both spread vegetatively, but buffalograss is much shorter and has very different male/female inflorescences.
